newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy sees year EPS above $0.46.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy sees year EPS above $0.46.

text.p: Best Buy Co Inc said Thursday that analysts' projections of a loss of $0.03 per share for its fiscal second quarter are similar to the company's expectations, but analysts' projections of a profit of $0.46 a share for the full year are too low.

"I think (a second quarter loss of $0.03 per share) is very close to what our expectations are," President and Chief Operating Officer Bradbury Anderson told Reuters after the specialty retailer's annual meeting here.

"We would consider (an earnings estimate of $0.46 per share for the year) on the low side," Anderson continued. "There are analysts in the $0.70 range, so we would consider ($0.46) a conservative number for the year."
According to First Call, analysts' estimates range from $0.15 to $0.70 a share, with $0.46 as the mean.
"We would be more comfortable with the higher side of that range," Anderson said.
Best Buy earned $0.09 a share for the year-ago second quarter, and $0.04 a share for the fiscal year ended March 1, 1997.
Anderson said Best Buy's revenues would have single-digit growth in fiscal 1998.

"Our total revenues for the year will be up slightly over last year, in the low-to-mid single digits," he said. "That includes an expectation of negative comps (comparable-store sales). We expect the first quarter had the greatest negative comps for the year. We expect comp-store sales to improve somewhat during the course of the year."
In April Best Buy said it expected comparable-store sales to decline in the first half, given soft demand for some products and the company's decision to focus on more profitable products.
In the first quarter, ended May 31, Best Buy's revenues declined 1.8 percent from a year earlier, to $1.607 billion, and comparable-store sales were down eight percent.

After the annual meeting, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Richard Schulze told Reuters the company is featuring cellular phones, pagers, electric car alarms, camcorders, and computers with CD-ROMs.
Schulze said Best Buy is testing demand for unspecified new products and would have an announcement in that regard after the second quarter ends in August.
Schulze told shareholders that Best Buy intends to increase its warranty service business as a portion of sales in fiscal year 1998.

"Our intention this year is to move performance service plans as a percentage of sales from two percent in fiscal year 1997 to something closer to three percent," he said. "Every one percentage point increase equates to a $0.50 increase in earnings per share."
